# English Language Style Guide

This guide provides conventions for writing clear, concise, and consistent English in text and markdown files. These guidelines are in addition to the guidelines established in the [`copilot-instructions.md`](../copilot-instructions.md) file.

## Document Audience
When writing or editing documents, write for an audience that is semi-technical. Assume that the reader has some familiarity with programming, but do not assume expert-level knowledge of language design or the implementation of compilers or interpreters. Do not assume that the reader has a formal Computer Science education. The reader of the interpreter documentation will have some prior C++ experience, but may not be a language expert.

## General Principles
- Use plain language and avoid jargon where possible.
- Prefer active voice over passive voice.
- Be concise. Eliminate unnecessary words.
- Be professional in tone and style.
- Limit the use of emojis to checkboxes and other functional elements, rather than decorative purposes. Use them sparingly and only when they add clear value to the content.

## Markdown Specific
- Use headings to structure content logically.
- Use lists for enumerations and steps.
- Use code blocks for code snippets.
- Use links for references and related content.
- Avoid excessive formatting. Keep it simple and readable.
- Use consistent heading levels and styles throughout the document.
